normalization.warning: Commercial products report nominal absorption capacity, while SCOBY scenarios below use 60% recovered-oil fraction. These are not perfectly equivalent metrics; the comparison is intentionally conservative for SCOBY on recovery but does not include commercial disposal/recovery costs.

scoby_optimistic_low_cost_byproduct_rout.interpretation: If SCOBY/KBC is genuinely sourced as a low-cost coproduct and processing remains simple, material cost becomes a small part of total cost; sleeve, drying, treatment, labor and retrieval then dominate.

closest_biobased_comparison.green_boom_notes: Commercially available bio-based hydrophobic marine boom; official Green Boom material states biomass-only renewable absorbents, and product literature supports wringing/reuse. This means SCOBY is not unique merely by being biodegradable or press-recoverable.
closest_biobased_comparison.scoby_required_advantage: Win on delivered cost, recovered-oil fraction, waste-stream feedstock, manufacturing simplicity, or measured marine performance rather than novelty alone.

janus_market_reverse.forward: LOW_COST_SCOBY_SOURCE -> PROCESS -> MARINE_q -> RETRIEVE -> PRESS_RECOVERY -> COST_PER_RECOVERED_KG -> MARKET_COMPARISON

preliminary_verdict.against_cheapest_PP: At central 14.8 USD/kg dry BC, q=20 g/g is not enough to confidently beat the cheapest current PP booms after processing; q around 40 g/g creates a plausible cost window. Low-cost waste-derived BC can shift break-even strongly in SCOBY's favor even near q=20 g/g.
preliminary_verdict.against_biobased_Green_Boom: SCOBY at q>=20 g/g has a plausible material-cost advantage under the central BC scenario, but total cost must still include drying, hydrophobicization, sleeve and retrieval. q>=40 g/g would create much stronger headroom.
preliminary_verdict.best_current_target: MARINE_q >= 40 g/g, press recovery >= 60%, retrieval >=99%, delivered processed cartridge cost normalized below about 1.25 USD per kg recovered oil to beat the cheapest listed PP on purchase-capacity economics, or below about 2.62 USD/kg to beat the listed Green Boom bio-based analogue.

next_measurement_gate: Run matched 50x50 and 100x100 tests against one cheap PP control and, if obtainable, one Green Boom biomass control under the same oil, water, drain and press-recovery protocol. Compare TOTAL_COST_PER_KG_RECOVERED_OIL rather than nominal capacity.
